plan.title: Single-stage RFQ required T&C blocks vendor submission

steps.note: Open the single-stage event creation screen.
Ensure clauses are not globally preselected as mandatory.
Enable event creation and the single-stage RFQ flow.
Allow a vendor to be added during event creation.
Set the event type to RFQ and award the entire lot to one vendor.
Provide the mandatory event title.
Apply the first available RFQ template so the pricing sheet can be configured.
Select the specified product in the pricing sheet.
Verify the requested product was selected.
Verify the product's mapped default variant filled automatically.
Enter the requested quantity.
Verify the quantity was retained.
Select the specified delivery location.
Verify the delivery location selection.
Complete any remaining required pricing-sheet fields before publishing.

args.goal: On the single-stage RFQ create screen, open Terms & Conditions, add the clauses "Payment within 45 days" and "Delivery within 7 days", set "Payment within 45 days" to Required, leave "Delivery within 7 days" as None, click Done, and stop on the create screen showing the configured event.

steps.note: Configure the two event-wise clauses and their required/optional modes, which no dedicated catalog step exposes.
a product is needed before participants or publishing
Add one QA test vendor without inventing a vendor name.
Commit the 30-minute event schedule.
Publish the configured RFQ.
Verify the event reached a published project page.
Move to the invited QA vendor's supplier portal session.
Open this event's RFQ pricing round as the vendor.
Verify the required clause is present in the vendor's terms block.
Verify the optional clause is present in the vendor's terms block.
Accept only the optional clause.
Attempt submission with the optional clause accepted but the required clause unaccepted; the vendor bid must be blocked.
Accept the required clause after the blocked submission.
Submit the vendor quote at 100 after all required terms are accepted.
Verify the vendor's bid was accepted and submitted.
